class DatabaseSettings(BaseSettings):
    """The one setting migrations need, so the migrate container never sees the JWT secret."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(extra="ignore", frozen=True, case_sensitive=False)

    database_url: PostgresDsn


class Settings(DatabaseSettings):
    """Everything the API reads from its environment."""

    jwt_secret: SecretStr = Field(min_length=32)
    app_origin: str = "http://localhost:8080"
    cookie_secure: bool = False
    log_level: Literal["DEBUG", "INFO", "WARNING", "ERROR"] = "INFO"
    db_pool_size: int = 10
    db_max_overflow: int = 5
    db_pool_timeout_seconds: float = 5.0

    @field_validator("app_origin")
    @classmethod
    def normalise_the_app_origin(cls, value: str) -> str:
        """Drop a trailing slash and require `scheme://host[:port]`, the exact form browsers send in Origin.

        A slash or a path would never equal a browser's Origin header, and every write would get 403
        (https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#origin-header).
        """
        origin = value.rstrip("/")
        parts = urlsplit(origin)
        if parts.scheme not in {"http", "https"} or not parts.hostname or parts.username or not has_a_valid_port(parts):
            raise ValueError("APP_ORIGIN must be http(s)://host[:port]")
        if parts.path or parts.query or parts.fragment:
            raise ValueError("APP_ORIGIN must not have a path, query or fragment")
        return origin

    @model_validator(mode="after")

todo-app · spec · revision 1 · for review

Round 2: the same app on a local Kubernetes cluster

The high-level choices for running the round 1 app on k3d, and how the pieces fit, before the detailed plan is written. The app code and images stay the same; what surrounds them changes. Each choice names what it beat and what it costs. Choices that follow from the kickoff, the round 1 spec or the deployment rule are locked; the rest are your call, listed again at the end.

__DATE__ · revision 1Lives at docs/specs/round-2.htmlBuilds on docs/specs/round-1.html and docs/kickoff.mdRules: .claude/rules/deployment.md
Round 1 · mergedContainersdocker compose up on a Mac. At least 1,000 users.
Round 2 · this specLocal k3dSame images, Kubernetes manifests, three API replicas on three nodes.
Round 3AKS liveAzure, deployed by GitHub Actions, if time permits.
TopologyDecisionsShutdownDeploy orderProving itTestsOrder of workRound 3Done meansYour calls
Solution diagram

One front door, three API pods on three nodes, one database

The browser talks to https://localhost:8443. k3s's built-in Traefik ends TLS and sends every request to the web pods. nginx in those pods does exactly what it does in compose: serves the SPA, sets the security headers and forwards /api/*. It reaches the API through a headless Service, which lists each pod, so every request is balanced across the three pods rather than pinned to one.

High-level choices

Decisions

Numbering continues from round 1 (D1 to D20). Locked ones follow from documents you already signed off. The calls are my recommendations.

D21

A three-node k3d cluster

your call
Choice
k3d 5.9.0 running k3s v1.36.4, one server and two agent nodes, from a config file at deploy/k3d/cluster.yaml. Port 8443 on the Mac maps to 443 on the cluster's load balancer. The three API pods are spread one per node.
Instead of
One node, which is lighter but puts every replica on one machine.
Why
Pods on different nodes talk over the cluster network, as they will on AKS. A node going away is something we can show, not only describe.
Costs
About 1.5 GB more of Docker's memory. Docker has 8 GB here, which is enough.
D22

One Kustomize base, one overlay per target

locked
Choice
deploy/base/ holds every resource once. deploy/overlays/k3d/ sets what differs locally: hostname, TLS secret name, image tags, sizes. Round 3 adds deploy/overlays/aks/.
Instead of
A Helm chart, or copied manifests per environment.
Why
Plain YAML you can read line by line, and kubectl builds it with no extra tool. The deployment rule asks for this shape.
D23

The same images, tagged with the commit

locked
Choice
The compose build makes todo-api:<sha> and todo-web:<sha>; k3d image import copies them onto every node. Pods never pull, so no registry is needed in round 2.
Instead of
A local registry, or images built separately for the cluster.
Why
What passed in compose is exactly what runs in k3d. Round 3 pushes the same images to Azure Container Registry.
D24

Postgres as a one-pod StatefulSet

locked
Choice
The same Postgres 18.6 image as compose, one pod with a volume from k3s's local-path storage.
Instead of
A Postgres operator with replicas and backups, such as CloudNativePG.
Why
Round 3 uses Azure's managed Postgres, which brings its own replicas and backups. An operator here would be built once and thrown away.
Costs
The database is a single pod. Losing its node loses the service until it comes back; the data survives on the volume.
D25

Migrations run as a Job, before the API rolls out

locked
Choice
A Job named migrate-<sha> runs alembic upgrade head with the API image and the database address alone. The deploy waits for it to complete, then rolls out the API.
Instead of
Running migrations at start-up in every pod, or in an init container.
Why
One run per release, never three pods racing to migrate. A failed migration stops the release before any pod changes.
D26

Three API pods that roll without dropping a request

locked
Choice
A Deployment with 3 replicas, one uvicorn process each. A rolling update adds a new pod before removing an old one, and a disruption budget keeps at least 2 serving. CPU and memory requests and limits are set; the CPU limit is one core, the most one uvicorn process can use. Probes: /livez for liveness, /readyz for readiness.
Instead of
More uvicorn workers per pod, which hides failures inside one pod and splits the connection budget unevenly.
Why
The round 1 spec planned 3 replicas and a budget of 45 connections for round 2. Scaling stays a replica count.
D27

nginx stays the front of the app; Traefik only ends TLS

your call
Choice
One Ingress sends everything to the web Service (2 nginx pods). nginx forwards /api/* to a headless API Service and re-reads its pod list from DNS, as it does in compose. The nginx image reads the DNS server and the API's address from its environment at start-up, through the image's own template step, so one image runs in both places.
Instead of
Traefik routing /api straight to the API. That needs the security headers, CSP, body limit and request id written a second time as Traefik middleware, and compose and k3d would no longer run the same front end. Or a normal Service, where nginx's kept-alive connections stick to one pod: the load skews and a rollout drains slowly.
Why
One nginx config, already tested by every suite, guards the app in all three rounds.
Costs
nginx learns about pod changes through DNS, up to about 15 seconds late. D29 covers that.
D28

TLS on k3d with a locally trusted certificate

your call
Choice
mkcert makes a certificate for localhost that this Mac trusts. You create it and load it as a TLS Secret. The cookie turns Secure, which the app allows only with a real JWT secret, never the example one. CI makes a throwaway certificate in the job.
Instead of
Traefik's own self-signed certificate: no setup, but the browser warns and the tests must skip certificate checks. Or plain HTTP until AKS: the simplest, but the Secure cookie, HTTPS origin and TLS ending would first be tried on Azure.
Why
The round 1 spec turns the cookie Secure once TLS exists. Rehearsing that locally finds a broken sign-in here rather than on AKS.
Costs
One brew install mkcert and mkcert -install, which adds a local certificate authority to the Mac's trust store. That is your step, and a reviewer's too.
D29

A pod leaves the rotation before it stops

your call
Choice
Each API pod has a 20-second preStop sleep, using Kubernetes's built-in sleep action so no shell is needed. Then uvicorn gets SIGTERM and finishes in-flight requests within its existing 20-second limit. The grace period is 45 seconds. The deployment rule's line "/readyz fails once shutdown starts" is replaced by this.
Instead of
Making /readyz fail after SIGTERM. Kubernetes already takes a terminating pod out of the Service the moment shutdown starts, so a failing probe adds nothing. The gap is DNS: nginx can keep sending to the pod for up to about 15 seconds, and only the sleep covers that.
Why
A rolling update or a killed pod should fail no requests. The timeline below shows why 20 seconds is enough.
D30

Settings in a ConfigMap; secrets you create

locked
Choice
A ConfigMap holds the origin, the cookie flag and the log level. You create two Secrets from commands I write out: one with the database password and the JWT secret, one with the TLS certificate. The pod builds DATABASE_URL from the password at start, so the password is stored once.
Instead of
Secrets committed in any form, including encrypted ones.
Why
The kickoff and the deployment rule: secrets are never in the repo, and I never see them. Round 3 moves them to Key Vault.
D31

Locked down by default

your call
Choice
The todo namespace enforces the restricted Pod Security level. Every pod runs as a non-root user with a read-only filesystem, drops every capability, uses the default seccomp profile and gets no service account token. Network policies deny all traffic, then allow only the arrows in the diagram.
Instead of
Kubernetes's defaults, where any pod can reach the database.
Why
It carries round 1's container hardening into the cluster, and the same manifests then meet AKS's stricter defaults.
Costs
Postgres under restricted needs its user and volume permissions set exactly. If the local-path volume refuses that, I'll stop and bring you the options rather than loosen it quietly.
D32

One deploy script, and every apply still asks you

your call
Choice
deploy/k3d/deploy.py (Python standard library) runs the order below for the README and CI. In this session I run the same steps one at a time, so each kubectl apply and delete asks you first, as the guard intends.
Instead of
Me running the script in the session, which would apply manifests without asking you for each one.
Why
A reviewer gets one command, and you keep the say over every change to a running cluster.
D33

A k3d job in CI

your call
Choice
A new CI job, run on every PR alongside e2e. It creates the cluster, deploys the PR's images with throwaway secrets (never printed), runs the live and browser suites, and runs a short k6 load with a rolling restart in the middle.
Instead of
Running k3d only on this Mac, or only on PRs that touch deploy/.
Why
A manifest or nginx change that breaks the cluster fails its own PR. Path filters make required checks hang on PRs they skip.
Costs
About 6 to 8 more minutes per PR, running at the same time as e2e.
Why D29 works

A pod leaves the rotation before it stops

When a pod is deleted, by a rolling update or by hand, Kubernetes removes it from the Service at once. nginx still holds the old pod list for up to about 15 seconds: its own 10-second re-read plus the cluster DNS's 5-second record lifetime. The pod keeps serving through that window, then drains.

Deploy order

Each step waits for the one before

StepWhat happensWho runs it
1k3d cluster create --config deploy/k3d/cluster.yaml: three nodes, port 8443Me, once you have reviewed the config
2Build the images with compose, then k3d image import them onto the nodesMe
3Create the namespace, then the two Secrets from the commands I give youYou
4Apply Postgres; wait until it is readyMe, and the apply asks you
5Apply the migrate-<sha> Job; wait until it completes. A failure stops hereMe, and the apply asks you
6Apply the API, web, Ingress and network policies; wait for each rollout to finishMe, and the apply asks you
7Check https://localhost:8443: the app loads, and API responses come from all three podsMe

Running the same commit again changes nothing: the Job already completed and the manifests match what is running. A new commit makes a new Job name and a new image tag, so it rolls.

Your round 1 point 3

Proving the API keeps nothing in memory

You asked in the round 1 review to prove that no replica holds state of its own, and moved it to this round. Each claim below has a run that would fail if it were false.

ClaimHow it is shownWhere
Any pod serves any requestOne signed-in session makes requests until all three pods (by X-Served-By) have answered, and each one sees the same tasksLive suite, every run
Losing a pod loses nothing200 users under load; an API pod is deleted. No request fails, and every user's tasks check out afterwardsk6, with you
A release drops no requestThe same load through a rolling restart of the APIk6, with you; CI repeats it on every PR
Nothing survives in pods, and nothing needs toEvery API pod is replaced while users are signed in. They stay signed in, and their tasks and order are intactk6, with you
Scaling is a numberScale the API from 3 to 5 pods and back under load; no request failsk6, with you
The database is fenced offA throwaway pod outside the allowed set tries to reach Postgres and times outShown once, with you
Tests

The same suites, a new address

Round 2 changes no app behaviour, so the unit and integration suites stay as they are. The stack-wide suites take the cluster's address and its certificate and run unchanged; each new test names a failure only the cluster can show.

LayerRound 2 change
Backend, frontendNone. Still run on every PR.
Live APIRuns against k3d as well as compose. Adds one test: a session reaches all three pods and each sees the same data.
Browser journeysThe same five journeys, run against k3d as well.
LoadThe same journey and budgets, run against k3d. Adds the disruption scenarios above and a stepped capacity run for the round's figure.
Order of work

Small PRs, each one reviewed

StepWhatYour gate
SThis specSign-off
AThe coding plan, docs/plans/round-2.mdSign-off
K1nginx reads its DNS server and API address from its environment; compose behaves as beforePR review
K2Cluster config, Kustomize base and k3d overlay, deploy script, README stepsG6: you review every manifest before the first apply
K3Suites pointed at k3d, the new live test, the disruption runsCP4: disruption runs with you
K4The k3d CI jobPR review
K5Capacity on k3d, recorded with round 1'sCP5: load run with you
G7Exit check on the round branch, then the parent PR into mainFinal review and merge
Looking ahead

What round 3 changes

The base manifests stay. The AKS overlay swaps Postgres for Azure Database for PostgreSQL (with its built-in PgBouncer, since round 3 adds a pod autoscaler), uses the cluster's managed ingress with a real certificate, pulls images from Azure Container Registry and reads secrets from Key Vault. GitHub Actions deploys it after signing in to Azure with OIDC, with no stored keys. You run or approve everything that touches Azure.

Exit criteria

Round 2 is done when

  • On a Mac with Docker Desktop and k3d, the README's steps create the cluster and deploy it. https://localhost:8443 serves the app, and the three API pods run on three different nodes.
  • The cluster runs the same commit-tagged images as compose, from one Kustomize base and a k3d overlay. You reviewed every manifest before it was first applied.
  • The migration Job completes before the API rolls out, and deploying the same commit again changes nothing.
  • The live and browser suites pass against k3d, and still pass against compose.
  • Under 200 users, deleting an API pod, a rolling restart and replacing every pod cause no failed request and no lost data; signed-in users stay signed in.
  • A pod outside the allowed set cannot reach Postgres, and no secret is in the repo.
  • The round's capacity figure on k3d is recorded next to round 1's.
  • CI runs the k3d job on every PR, and it is green.
  • The README has a section for running on k3d.
For your review

Your calls

My recommendation comes first in each. Reply by number, as in round 1.

  1. Cluster shape (D21). Three nodes with the API spread across them, or one node.
  2. Front door (D27). nginx stays the front of the app and Traefik only ends TLS, or Traefik routes /api itself.
  3. TLS on k3d (D28). A trusted mkcert certificate, Traefik's self-signed one, or plain HTTP until AKS.
  4. Shutdown (D29). A preStop sleep, with the deployment rule's readiness line replaced, or keep the rule and add the probe change as well.
  5. Hardening (D31). Restricted Pod Security and default-deny network policies, or Kubernetes's defaults for now.
  6. Deploying (D32). One script for the README and CI, with each apply run on its own in this session so it asks you.
  7. CI (D33). A k3d job on every PR, or k3d on this Mac only.
Revision 1, for the lead's review. Sign-off and your notes are recorded here and in docs/kickoff.md, as in round 1.

content.text:
The round 2 spec is ready for your review: https://claude.ai/artifact/JMGPHpioK4KaprBL8GuCo3

It's private, and also saved at `docs/specs/round-2.html` on `docs/round-2-spec`. I haven't committed it; it goes in once you sign off, as the round 1 spec did. `round/2-k3d` matches `main`, and k3d 5.9.0 with k3s v1.36.4 is ready.

**What's in it:**
- **Topology diagram:** Traefik ends TLS and passes traffic to nginx. nginx balances each `/api` request across 3 API pods, one per node. Postgres is a single-pod StatefulSet, and the migration Job must finish before the API rolls out.
- **Decisions D21 to D33**, numbered on from round 1:
  - **Locked**, from documents you already signed off: the Kustomize base with a k3d overlay, the same commit-tagged images, the Postgres StatefulSet, the migration Job, 3 replicas within the 45-connection budget, and Secrets you create.
  - **Your call:** the other seven decisions.
- **Proof plan for your round 1 point 3** (no API pod keeps state of its own). One run per claim, each of which would fail if the claim were false:
  - one session reaches all three pods;
  - an API pod is deleted under load;
  - a rolling restart;
  - every pod replaced while users are signed in;
  - scaling from 3 to 5 pods and back;
  - a pod outside the app can't reach the database.
- **Order of work:** K1 to K5, with your gates G6 (manifest review before the first apply), CP4 (disruption runs), CP5 (capacity) and G7 (exit check).
- **Exit criteria:** nine of them.

**Correction to what I said earlier:** I told you `/readyz` needed fixing so it fails once shutdown starts. It doesn't. Kubernetes already takes a terminating pod out of the Service as soon as shutdown starts. The real gap is that nginx can keep a stale pod list for up to about 15 seconds. A 20-second sleep before the pod stops covers that, and the spec has a timeline showing why (D29). Doing it this way means changing a line in the deployment rule, so it's your call 4, not a silent change.

**Your calls, my recommendation first.** Reply by number, as in round 1:
1. **Cluster shape:** three nodes with the API spread across them, or one node.
2. **Front door:** nginx stays in front of the app and Traefik only ends TLS, or Traefik routes `/api` itself.
3. **TLS on k3d:** a trusted mkcert certificate (one `brew install` plus `mkcert -install`, your step), Traefik's self-signed one, or plain HTTP until AKS.
4. **Shutdown:** the 20-second sleep with the rule's readiness line replaced, or keep the rule and change the probe as well.
5. **Hardening:** restricted Pod Security and default-deny network policies, or Kubernetes's defaults.
6. **Deploying:** one script for the README and CI. When I deploy in this session, I run each `kubectl apply` on its own so you approve every one.
7. **CI:** a k3d job on every PR (about 6 to 8 extra minutes, running alongside e2e), or k3d on this Mac only.

**Size after sign-off:** the plan, then 5 child PRs with about 15 to 20 manifest files, 1 nginx change and 1 deploy script, over a few sessions. External waits come on top: CI, your G6 review, and the CP4 and CP5 runs with you.

content.text:
Short version: a **node is a machine, not a service.** The backend and frontend already scale separately, but they do it as **pods**, each with its own replica count. Nodes are a shared pool of machines that Kubernetes places those pods on.

### Three layers

| Thing | What it is | In our k3d cluster |
|---|---|---|
| **Container** | One running image: an nginx, a uvicorn, a Postgres | `todo-api:<sha>`, `todo-web:<sha>`, `postgres:18.6` |
| **Pod** | One or more containers scheduled together; the unit Kubernetes scales and replaces | One container each: an `api` pod, a `web` pod, `postgres-0` |
| **Node** | A machine with CPU and memory that runs pods. On AKS it's a VM; in k3d it's a Docker container pretending to be a machine | `server-0`, `agent-0`, `agent-1` |

**Scaling happens at the pod level.** The API has its own Deployment with `replicas: 3`, and the web has its own with `replicas: 2`. You can change either without touching the other: `kubectl scale deployment/api --replicas=5` adds API pods and leaves the web alone. That gives you the separate backend and frontend scaling you're after, without tying either one to a node.

### The two node types
- **Server node** (Kubernetes calls this the *control plane*): the cluster's brain.
  - It runs the Kubernetes API that `kubectl` talks to, and the scheduler that decides which node each pod goes on.
  - It stores the cluster's state and runs the controllers that keep reality matching the manifests. For example, it starts a new pod when one dies.
  - In k3s a server can also run app pods.
- **Agent node** (a *worker*): just muscle. It runs pods it's given and reports back. It makes no decisions.

On AKS it's the same split, except Azure runs the control plane for you and hides it. You only see and pay for the worker nodes.

### What I proposed, and why
```
server-0 (control plane + workloads)   agent-0              agent-1
├─ api                                 ├─ api               ├─ api
├─ web                                 ├─ web               └─ postgres-0
└─ traefik                             └─ …
```
- **Three nodes** so the 3 API pods land on three different machines, one each. Then "a node goes away and the app keeps serving" is something we can actually show, and pods talk across the cluster network as they will on AKS.
- **Which pod goes on which node is left to the scheduler,** with one rule: spread the API pods across nodes. Web pods go wherever there's room.

### On your idea: one node per tier
Kubernetes can do that. You label nodes (say `tier=web` and `tier=api`) and tell each Deployment to use only its own nodes. On AKS these are called **node pools**, and each pool can autoscale on its own. Teams use them when tiers need different hardware or strict isolation: GPU nodes, memory-heavy databases, or noisy jobs kept away from the API.

For this app I'd **not** split by tier:
- **No resilience gain:** with one API node, losing that node takes down every API pod at once, which is the opposite of what the spread buys.
- **Wasted capacity:** nginx uses under a tenth of a core, so a whole node for it sits mostly empty.
- **Separate scaling already works** at the pod level, as above.

A split that *does* earn its place comes in round 3: AKS's standard **system pool** (cluster add-ons) plus a **user pool** (our app), with the user pool autoscaling.

Do you want to keep the shared, spread layout? Or should I add tier-labelled nodes to k3d so the node-pool idea is visible there too? Either way, I'll add this explanation to the D21 section in the spec.

content.text:
Not quite. The nodes aren't split by part of the app. "Server" and "agent" are k3s's names for the two kinds of machine in a cluster:

| Node | What it is | What runs on it |
|---|---|---|
| **server-0** | The **control plane**: the Kubernetes API you talk to with `kubectl`, the scheduler that decides where pods go, and the cluster's own store | The control plane, plus ordinary app pods. k3s lets a server run app pods by default |
| **agent-0**, **agent-1** | **Worker nodes**. They only run pods | App pods, wherever the scheduler puts them |

In k3d, each node is just a Docker container on your Mac: `k3d-todo-server-0`, `k3d-todo-agent-0` and `k3d-todo-agent-1`. A fourth container, `k3d-todo-serverlb`, is k3d's small load balancer. It forwards `localhost:8443` into the cluster.

**There's no "frontend node" or "database node".** I tell the scheduler what each part needs, and it picks the nodes. The one rule in the spec is that the 3 API pods are spread **one per node**, so a typical layout looks like this:

| | server-0 | agent-0 | agent-1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| API | api pod | api pod | api pod |
| Web (nginx) | | web pod | web pod |
| Postgres | | postgres-0 | |
| Cluster add-ons | Traefik, DNS | | |

The web pods and Postgres could land elsewhere. Wherever they go, the API is always on all three nodes.

**Why this shape:**
- **The API on three nodes:** losing a node, or a node being restarted, still leaves two API pods serving. Requests between pods also cross the cluster network, as they will on AKS.
- **No dedicated nodes:** AKS works the same way. Azure runs the control plane and hides it, and you only see worker nodes. If we tied parts of the app to particular nodes now, round 3 would have to undo it.

**One catch, about Postgres.** k3s's local storage keeps the database's data on whichever node Postgres first starts on, and the pod is then tied to that node. If that node goes down, Postgres waits for it rather than moving, though the data stays safe on the node. That's fine for a laptop, and it's the "single pod" cost already noted in D24. On AKS, Azure's managed Postgres removes it.

You could pin Postgres to a node of its own, like a database node pool on AKS. I'd recommend against it for round 2: it adds a node to manage and changes nothing we're proving.

I can add a short version of this to D21 in the spec, so the reader doesn't need this explanation.

# The stack: `docker compose up --build --wait`, then open http://localhost:8080.
# Values come from .env (copy .env.example); a missing one stops compose before anything starts.

# Shared by the app containers: nothing on the image's filesystem can change at run time, no Linux
# capabilities, and no way to gain privileges (https://docs.docker.com/reference/compose-file/services/).
x-hardening: &hardening
  read_only: true
  tmpfs: [/tmp]
  cap_drop: [ALL]
  security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]

x-database-url: &database-url postgresql+asyncpg://${POSTGRES_USER:?set POSTGRES_USER in .env, see .env.example}:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env, see .env.example}@db:5432/${POSTGRES_DB:?set POSTGRES_DB in .env, see .env.example}

services:
  db:
    image: postgres:18.6-alpine3.24
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER:?set POSTGRES_USER in .env, see .env.example}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env, see .env.example}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB:?set POSTGRES_DB in .env, see .env.example}
    volumes:
      # Postgres 18 images keep PGDATA at /var/lib/postgresql/18/docker, under this mount
      # (https://hub.docker.com/_/postgres). A mount at the old .../data path would lose data on re-create.
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U $$POSTGRES_USER -d $$POSTGRES_DB"]
      interval: 5s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 10s

  # Runs the migrations once, then exits; the API starts only after it exits with 0.
  # It gets the database URL alone, never the JWT secret.
  migrate:
    <<: *hardening
    # The api service builds this image; two services building one tag would clash on export.
    image: todo-api:${GIT_SHA:-local}
    pull_policy: never
    command: ["alembic", "upgrade", "head"]
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: *database-url
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
    restart: "no"

  # Two replicas behind nginx; any replica can serve any request. Reachable only inside the compose network.
  api:
    <<: *hardening
    build: ./backend
    image: todo-api:${GIT_SHA:-local}
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: *database-url
      JWT_SECRET: ${JWT_SECRET:?set JWT_SECRET in .env, see .env.example}
      APP_ORIGIN: ${APP_ORIGIN:?set APP_ORIGIN in .env, see .env.example}
      COOKIE_SECURE: ${COOKIE_SECURE:?set COOKIE_SECURE in .env, see .env.example}
      LOG_LEVEL: ${LOG_LEVEL:?set LOG_LEVEL in .env, see .env.example}
    depends_on:
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
    deploy:
      replicas: 2
    expose: ["8000"]
    # Longer than uvicorn's 20 s drain, so in-flight requests finish before Docker kills the process.
    stop_grace_period: 25s
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "python", "-c", "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8000/readyz', timeout=2)"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # nginx: the SPA and the proxy to the API. The stack's one published port, bound to the loopback address only.
  web:
    <<: *hardening
    build: ./frontend
    image: todo-web:${GIT_SHA:-local}
    depends_on:
      api:
        condition: service_healthy
    ports: ["127.0.0.1:8080:8080"]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-q", "--spider", "http://127.0.0.1:8080/"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s

"""Values and helpers the live tests share."""

from typing import Final
from uuid import uuid4

# The stack's one published port, where nginx serves the SPA and proxies the API.
BASE_URL: Final = "http://localhost:8080"
PASSWORD: Final = "correct horse battery staple"


def unique_email() -> str:
    """Return an address no earlier run has registered, so tests never share an account."""
    return f"live-{uuid4().hex}@example.com"
"""Shared fixtures for the live tests."""

from collections.abc import Iterator

import httpx
import pytest

from support import BASE_URL


@pytest.fixture
def client() -> Iterator[httpx.Client]:
    """Yield a client that talks to the stack the way the browser does: through nginx, from the app's origin."""
    with httpx.Client(base_url=BASE_URL, headers={"Origin": BASE_URL}, timeout=10.0) as live_client:
        yield live_client

def test_api_docs_are_served_through_the_proxy(client: httpx.Client) -> None:
    page = client.get("/api/docs")
    document = client.get("/api/openapi.json")

    assert (page.status_code, page.headers["content-type"].split(";")[0]) == (200, "text/html")
    assert (document.status_code, document.json()["info"]["title"]) == (200, "todo-app API")


def test_session_from_one_replica_is_accepted_by_the_other(client: httpx.Client) -> None:
    client.post("/api/v1/auth/register", json={"email": unique_email(), "password": PASSWORD})

    # nginx spreads requests over the replicas, so a few dozen calls reach both.
    answers = [client.get("/api/v1/auth/me") for _ in range(40)]

    assert {answer.status_code for answer in answers} == {200}
    assert len({answer.headers["x-served-by"] for answer in answers}) == 2


SECURITY_HEADERS = {
    "x-content-type-options": "nosniff",
    "referrer-policy": "strict-origin-when-cross-origin",
    "x-frame-options": "DENY",
    "permissions-policy": "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()",
    "cross-origin-opener-policy": "same-origin",
}


def test_security_headers_are_set_on_the_spa(client: httpx.Client) -> None:
    response = client.get("/")

    assert {name: response.headers.get(name) for name in SECURITY_HEADERS} == SECURITY_HEADERS
    # httpx joins repeated headers with ", ", so a second CSP would hide inside the first; count them instead.
    assert len(response.headers.get_list("content-security-policy")) == 1
    assert "default-src 'self'" in response.headers["content-security-policy"]
    assert "frame-ancestors 'none'" in response.headers["content-security-policy"]
    assert response.headers["cache-control"] == "no-cache"
    assert response.headers["server"] == "nginx"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("probe", ["/livez", "/readyz"])
def test_probes_are_not_reachable_through_the_front_door(client: httpx.Client, probe: str) -> None:
    assert client.get(probe).status_code == 404


def test_body_over_64_kb_is_rejected_at_the_proxy(client: httpx.Client) -> None:
    oversized = b"x" * (64 * 1024 + 1)

    response = client.post("/api/v1/tasks", content=oversized, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})

    assert response.status_code == 413
    assert "x-served-by" not in response.headers


def test_api_docs_csp_allows_the_inline_script_the_page_serves(client: httpx.Client) -> None:
    page = client.get("/api/docs")

    [inline_script] = re.findall(r"<script>(.*?)</script>", page.text, re.DOTALL)
    digest = base64.b64encode(hashlib.sha256(inline_script.encode()).digest()).decode()
    assert len(page.headers.get_list("content-security-policy")) == 1
    assert f"'sha256-{digest}'" in page.headers["content-security-policy"]


async def fire_moves_through_both_replicas(moves: int, seed: int) -> tuple[list[httpx.Response], list[str], list[str]]:
    """Sign up, create ten tasks, then send every move at once; return the answers, task ids and listed ids."""
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(base_url=BASE_URL, headers={"Origin": BASE_URL}, timeout=30.0) as client:
        await client.post("/api/v1/auth/register", json={"email": unique_email(), "password": PASSWORD})
        task_ids = [(await client.post("/api/v1/tasks", json={"title": f"task {n}"})).json()["id"] for n in range(10)]
        pick = random.Random(seed)
        pairs = [pick.sample(task_ids, 2) for _ in range(moves)]
        async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as group:
            sent = [
                group.create_task(client.put(f"/api/v1/tasks/{task}/position", json={"afterId": after}))
                for task, after in pairs
            ]
        listed = (await client.get("/api/v1/tasks")).json()["items"]
    return [move.result() for move in sent], task_ids, [item["rank"] for item in listed]


def test_concurrent_moves_through_both_replicas_keep_ranks_unique() -> None:
    answers, task_ids, ranks = asyncio.run(fire_moves_through_both_replicas(moves=50, seed=7))

    assert {answer.status_code for answer in answers} == {200}
    assert len({answer.headers["x-served-by"] for answer in answers}) == 2
    assert len(ranks) == len(set(ranks)) == len(task_ids)

        await client.post("/api/v1/auth/register", json={"email": unique_email(), "password": PASSWORD})
        task_ids = [(await client.post("/api/v1/tasks", json={"title": f"task {n}"})).json()["id"] for n in range(10)]
        pick = random.Random(seed)
        pairs = [pick.sample(task_ids, 2) for _ in range(moves)]
        async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as group:
            sent = [
                group.create_task(client.put(f"/api/v1/tasks/{task}/position", json={"afterId": after}))
                for task, after in pairs
            ]
        listed = (await client.get("/api/v1/tasks")).json()["items"]
    return [move.result() for move in sent], task_ids, [item["rank"] for item in listed]


def test_concurrent_moves_through_both_replicas_keep_ranks_unique() -> None:
    answers, task_ids, ranks = asyncio.run(fire_moves_through_both_replicas(moves=50, seed=7))

    assert {answer.status_code for answer in answers} == {200}
    assert len({answer.headers["x-served-by"] for answer in answers}) == 2
    assert len(ranks) == len(set(ranks)) == len(task_ids)

# frontend

React 19 SPA in TypeScript (Vite 8, React Router 8, TanStack Query 5, Tailwind 4, Zod 4, dnd-kit). Views take props and render; a container per route in `src/pages/` feeds each view from TanStack Query.

## Commands

```bash
npm ci                       # Node 24
npm run dev                  # the app on Vite's dev server; `/api` goes to the stack on :8080, so start it first
npm run check                # ESLint (type-checked) + prettier --check + tsc --noEmit
npm run test                 # Vitest + coverage; fails under 85% lines, branches, functions or statements
npm run build                # tsc, then the app into dist/
npm run design:dev           # the design gallery on Vite's dev server
npm run design:build         # the gallery as one self-contained file: design/dist/artifact.html
npm run design:screenshots   # after design:build; needs `npx playwright install chromium` once
```

Every commit passes `check`, `test` and `build`.

## Layout

- `src/main.tsx`: boot. The Zod config first, then one query client, the router, and the `[app] started` line.
- `src/app/`: the route table and the ended-session redirect (`router.tsx`), the signed-in guard (`require-auth.tsx`), and the route error boundary (`route-error.tsx`).
- `src/pages/`: one container per route. Hooks in, one view out, no markup of its own.
- `src/styles/tokens.css`: every colour, size, radius, shadow and duration, as Tailwind `@theme` tokens. The default theme is cleared, so a utility off the scale (`p-5`, `bg-red-500`) does not exist.
- `src/styles/index.css`: Tailwind, fonts, the `binding` and `ruled` utilities, and the hover, focus-visible and active variants the gallery can force.
- `src/components/ui/`: primitives. `src/components/`: compositions (`AppShell`, `AuthLayout`, `CredentialsForm`).
- `src/views/`: one view per screen. Props in, JSX out: no fetching, no router hooks, every intent leaves as a callback. Only local affordances (a draft, an open confirm) live in `useState`.
- `src/lib/api/`: the fetch wrapper (`apiRequest`, `ApiError` with a closed set of codes) and one function per endpoint. Every request goes through it.
- `src/lib/query/`: query keys, the query client (the one place a 401 is handled), and the hooks for auth and tasks. Toggle, move and delete share `optimisticListUpdate`.
- `src/lib/auth/auth-context.tsx`: `useAuth`, the session and the sign-in, sign-up and sign-out actions.
- `src/lib/`: pure helpers (`tasks/order.ts`, `task-draft.ts`, `task-list.ts`, `due-date.ts`), `routes.ts` with `signInPath`, and `schema/` (Zod, shared by forms and the API layer, URL params included).
- `src/hooks/`: `useDebouncedValue`.
- `src/test/fixtures.ts`: the sample data and view props that both the tests and the gallery use.
- `src/test/server.ts`, `handlers.ts`: MSW at the `fetch` boundary, answering from the fixtures. `render-app.tsx` renders the whole app at a path, wired like `main.tsx`.
- `Dockerfile`, `nginx.conf`: the stack's front door. nginx serves `dist/`, proxies `/api/` to the API replicas, sets the security headers and the CSP, caps request bodies at 64 KB, and answers 404 on `/livez` and `/readyz`.
- `design/`: the gallery, a second Vite entry. `screens.tsx` lists every state; `Scripted` drives a view the way a user would to reach states held in local state. `screenshots/` is committed.

## Gotchas

- `light-dark()` colours are polyfilled by Tailwind's Lightning CSS pass, so a theme switches only at the root (`color-scheme` on `:root`). Light-mode focus on the green band is too faint, so anything on the band sits in the `binding` utility, which turns the ring gilt.
- Layout responds to container width (`@wide:`), not the viewport. A view needs an `@container` ancestor; `Page`, `AppShell` and `AuthLayout` provide one.
- The gallery build roots Vite at `design/`, so `index.css` names `src/` and `design/` as Tailwind sources explicitly.
- Vitest stubs CSS imports; only `tokens.css` is processed, so the token tests can read it.
- `data-hover`, `data-focus-visible` and `data-active` exist for the gallery only. Never set them in app code.
- The design build inlines everything; the app build must not inline anything (the nginx CSP is `'self'` only).
- Zod runs `jitless`, set in `src/lib/schema/zod-config.ts`. Otherwise it probes for eval when a schema is built, and the CSP reports a violation on every page load. `main.tsx` imports that file first; keep it first, before any module that builds a schema.
- The CSP for `/api/docs` allows Swagger UI's one inline script by its hash. A FastAPI upgrade can change that script; the live test on the docs CSP then fails, and the hash in `nginx.conf` needs updating.
- The dev server sends `/api` to `http://localhost:8080` with that as its `Origin`, because the API refuses writes from any other origin. When port 5173 is taken, Vite moves to the next free port, so open the URL it prints, or choose one with `npm run dev -- --port <n>`.
- A request with no MSW handler fails the test. Add one with `server.use` in the test; handlers reset after each test.
- The query cache logs only failures that mean something broke (5xx, no connection, a response that doesn't match its schema) with `console.error`; expected 4xx answers are not logged. A test that expects such a failure silences it with `vi.spyOn(console, "error")`; spies are restored after each test.
- `useAuth` reads the `me` query in the component that calls it, not from context. Context only updates when its provider renders again, so a page reading it could act on a session that has already ended.
- A query that throws to the route error boundary keeps its error cached. The boundary calls `useQueryErrorResetBoundary().reset()` before retrying, or the old error is thrown again without a fetch.
- Moves share the mutation scope `task-order`, so they reach the server in the order they were made, and the lists refetch only after the last one.
- A mutation whose `onSettled` returns a promise stays pending until it settles. Toggle does not await its refetch, so a failure shows at once. Quick add does, so the new row replaces the pending one.
- In jsdom, dnd-kit keeps the row positions it measured first. A test that makes several keyboard moves (`src/test/drag.ts`) reads where tasks landed from the screen.
- `npm ci` from the committed lockfile works with the npm that ships with Node 24. Regenerating the lockfile from scratch crashes that npm (11.5.1) in arborist ("reading 'edgesOut'"), so change dependencies with `npx npm@11.21.0 install`, then confirm a clean `npm ci` with the default npm.
- Dependencies are pinned to exact versions, each published at least two weeks before it was chosen (plan § 13). A newer version needs a reason: a fix or an advisory. TanStack Query 5.104.2 was taken early for its fix to scoped mutations pausing in a hidden tab.

# Deployment

## Stages, in order
1. **Containers**: each service builds its own image; `docker compose up` runs the stack (database, backend, frontend). The whole test pyramid passes here first.
2. **Local Kubernetes**: a k3d cluster runs the same images from the same manifests, with more than one backend replica. Development continues here once stage 1 is proven.
3. **AKS**: an Azure Kubernetes Service cluster, deployed by GitHub Actions, only after stage 2 works end to end and the human signs off.

Do not start a stage before the previous one is proven and the human says go.

## The human reviews every deployment artifact
- Dockerfiles, compose files, Kubernetes manifests, overlays and workflows are shown to the human and approved before they are applied or merged. Show the file and say what it will create or change.
- The agent never applies anything to AKS or any shared cloud resource. It prepares the change and the exact command; the human runs it (`CONTRIBUTING.md` § 11). `kubectl apply`, `kubectl delete`, `helm` and `az` always ask, even against k3d.

## Built for more than one replica
- One uvicorn process per container; scale with replicas, never with in-container workers.
- The backend is stateless: auth is a signed token checked on every request, with no in-memory sessions or caches that requests write to. Any replica can serve any request.
- One set of manifests (Kustomize base) with one overlay per target (`k3d`, `aks`). No copy-pasted manifests per environment.
- Images are tagged with the git sha, never `latest`, and the same image moves from one stage to the next.
- Migrations run once per release as a Job before the backend rolls out, never from every pod at startup.
- Every backend pod has a liveness probe (`/livez`, process up, checks no dependencies) and a readiness probe (`/readyz`, database reachable, fails once shutdown starts). Neither is routed by nginx or the ingress. Requests and limits are set. Containers run as a non-root user with a read-only root filesystem where the runtime allows.
- Config comes from env vars through ConfigMaps; secrets come from Kubernetes Secrets the human creates. Neither is ever committed.

## The compose stack
- The `migrate` service runs the migrations once; the API starts only after it exits with 0. It gets the database URL alone, never the JWT secret.
- Two API replicas sit behind nginx. nginx publishes the only port, `127.0.0.1:8080`, and returns 404 for the probes.
- The app containers run read-only with every capability dropped. They set no CPU or memory limits yet.
- Images are tagged `todo-api:${GIT_SHA}` and `todo-web:${GIT_SHA}`, or `local` when `GIT_SHA` is unset. Set it on every compose command.
- Settings come from `.env`; compose stops before anything starts when one is missing.

CP3 ran with the lead present: the 200-user run and every step to 1,000 users met all budgets with no failed request. The round-1 capacity figure is **at least 1,000 concurrent users**, the highest step tested, on the machine recorded in `load/results/`; the lead chose not to push past it to find the ceiling. Results and their reading are in `load/results/round-1.md`.

## 5i. Containers merged, and the README's scope for now (verbatim)

> SQ&M#10 - done!
>
> Have a quick point here, just to keep our folder tree clean. Should we push all the tests into one folder? The common tests, as in the overall tests like E2E and load. And should we name those folders more explicitly, like load could be load test instead, or if it all goes inside the test folder, then it's fine. It's pretty self-explanatory. That's just one recommendation I have.
>
> To be honest, I don't think we write the thorough readme right now. And as in, we don't worry about the future section right now, because we're not really done with our work. We still have to do at least round two before we proceed further and think about wrapping this assignment up. And yeah, it's more about agent time here. And we have to take into account human review time as well. So yeah, we'll discuss this later.

What it settled: the stack-wide suites live under `tests/` (`tests/e2e/live`, `tests/e2e/browser`, `tests/load`), done in #10; each app's own tests stay in the app. Round 1's README covers running the stack and its tests on a Mac and the capacity figure, nothing more. The full write-up the brief asks for (approach, features, more time, robustness) waits until at least round 2 is done. When it is written, "how long it would have taken" is given in agent-pair time with the human review time counted in, not as human-solo days.

## 6. Before submission

- [ ] Share the spec artifact, and the design artifact, so the reviewers can open them; put the links in the final report.
- [ ] Run the load test (D18) with the lead, and quote its results and each round's capacity figure in the README.
- [ ] Export the session transcripts from `.ai-transcripts/` into `docs/ai-usage/` after a secrets and personal-data scan; write the human-versus-agent time split.
- [x] The GitHub repository is public (created public on 2026-10-18, at the lead's request).
# Future work

Ideas we chose not to build in rounds 1 to 3, and why each is worth doing. The README's "given more time" section draws from this list.

## Identity
- **Sign-in with Microsoft, Google or Apple.** OpenID Connect through the provider each client already uses (Microsoft Entra ID for a Microsoft shop, Google or Apple for consumers). Email and password stay as the fallback.
- **Refresh-token rotation and revocation.** Short-lived access tokens, a rotating refresh token, and a deny list, so a stolen or signed-out session can be ended before it expires.
- **Email verification and password reset.** Both need an outbound email service.

## AI features (after everything else works)
- **Create and update tasks by describing them.** The user types or speaks ("move the dentist to Friday and add a note to bring the form") and the app turns that into task creates and updates. The model's output is untrusted: it is parsed into the same typed models the API already validates, and the user confirms the changes before they are applied.
- **An AI summary home page.** A home screen that summarises what is due, overdue and done, streamed to the client, possibly built on the AG-UI protocol for agent-to-UI events.

## Data and scale
- **Rank rebalancing.** A background job that rewrites long ranks in a list to short ones, run when a rank passes a length limit.
- **Paging for long lists.** A cursor on `GET /api/v1/tasks`; the `{"items": [...]}` envelope already leaves room for it.
- **Sign-in rate limiting.** It needs a store shared by every replica (Redis, or the ingress), so it waits for round 2 or 3.

## Security
- **Self-host the API docs page, or turn it off in production.** `/api/docs` loads Swagger UI from jsDelivr under a floating major version, with no integrity check, and its CSP allows one inline script by hash. Serving pinned Swagger UI files from the API, or disabling the page where cookies are secure, removes the third-party script before the app is public.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Deploy the app to a local k3d cluster: `python3 deploy/k3d/deploy.py up`, then open https://localhost:8443.

`up` creates the cluster if it is missing, builds and imports the images for the current commit, creates the
secrets if they are missing, then applies Postgres, the migration Job and the app, each after the one before is
ready. `build`, `render` and `secrets` run one of those steps alone; `down` deletes the cluster and its data.
Every command is printed before it runs. Secret values reach kubectl on stdin and are never printed or kept.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
import secrets
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
CLUSTER = "todo"
NAMESPACE = "todo"
CLUSTER_CONFIG = "deploy/k3d/cluster.yaml"
PARTS = ("platform", "migrate", "app")
# Each image and the folder it is built from, the same build compose runs.
IMAGES = {"todo-api": "backend", "todo-web": "frontend"}
SHORT_SHA = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{7,40}")
# The browser's address, and the name k6 uses to reach the cluster from inside Docker.
CERT_NAMES = ("localhost", "127.0.0.1", "::1", "host.docker.internal")
TOOLS = ("docker", "k3d", "kubectl", "mkcert")
URL = "https://localhost:8443"


def release_files(sha: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Return the kustomization for each part of a release, keyed by its path under `deploy/.release/<sha>/`.

    Each part builds on its k3d overlay and pins both images to the commit. The migration Job's name also
    carries the commit, so each release runs it once and a repeat deploy of the same commit changes nothing.
    """
    if not SHORT_SHA.fullmatch(sha):
        raise ValueError(f"not a short lowercase git sha: {sha!r}")
    images = "".join(f"  - name: {name}\n    newTag: {sha}\n" for name in IMAGES)

    def kustomization(part: str) -> str:
        suffix = f"nameSuffix: -{sha}\n" if part == "migrate" else ""
        return (
            "apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1\nkind: Kustomization\n"
            f"resources:\n  - ../../../overlays/k3d/{part}\n{suffix}images:\n{images}"
        )

    return {f"{part}/kustomization.yaml": kustomization(part) for part in PARTS}


def rollout_steps(sha: str) -> list[list[str]]:
    """Return the kubectl commands that roll out a written release, each waiting for the one before."""
    release = f"deploy/.release/{sha}"
    namespace = ["-n", NAMESPACE]
    return [
        ["kubectl", "apply", "-k", f"{release}/platform"],
        ["kubectl", "rollout", "status", "statefulset/db", *namespace, "--timeout=180s"],
        ["kubectl", "apply", "-k", f"{release}/migrate"],
        ["kubectl", "wait", "--for=condition=complete", f"job/migrate-{sha}", *namespace, "--timeout=180s"],
        ["kubectl", "apply", "-k", f"{release}/app"],
        ["kubectl", "rollout", "status", "deployment/api", *namespace, "--timeout=300s"],
        ["kubectl", "rollout", "status", "deployment/web", *namespace, "--timeout=180s"],
    ]


def create_secret(name: str, data: dict[str, str], kind: str = "Opaque") -> tuple[list[str], str]:
    """Return the command that creates a Secret and the manifest to send on its stdin, so no value is an argument."""
    manifest = {
        "apiVersion": "v1",
        "kind": "Secret",
        "metadata": {"name": name, "namespace": NAMESPACE},
        "type": kind,
        "stringData": data,
    }
    return ["kubectl", "create", "-f", "-"], json.dumps(manifest)


def run(command: list[str], stdin: str | None = None) -> None:
    """Print the command, run it from the repo root, and stop the deploy if it fails."""
    print("+ " + " ".join(command), file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
    subprocess.run(command, cwd=REPO, input=stdin, text=True, check=True)


def succeeds(command: list[str]) -> bool:
    """Run a read-only check quietly and say whether it succeeded."""
    return subprocess.run(command, cwd=REPO, capture_output=True).returncode == 0


def current_sha() -> str:
    """Return the short sha of the checked-out commit, the tag compose gives its images too."""
    return subprocess.run(
        ["git", "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"], cwd=REPO, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True
    ).stdout.strip()


def require_tools() -> None:
    """Stop with the install command when a tool the deploy needs is missing."""
    missing = [tool for tool in TOOLS if shutil.which(tool) is None]
    if missing:
        sys.exit(f"missing {', '.join(missing)}: brew install {' '.join(missing)} (see the README)")


def ensure_cluster() -> None:
    """Create the three-node cluster unless it already exists."""
    if not succeeds(["k3d", "cluster", "get", CLUSTER]):
        run(["k3d", "cluster", "create", "--config", CLUSTER_CONFIG])


def build(sha: str) -> None:
    """Build both images for the commit and copy them onto every node, so no pod pulls from a registry."""
    tags = [f"{name}:{sha}" for name in IMAGES]
    for tag, folder in zip(tags, IMAGES.values()):
        run(["docker", "build", "-t", tag, folder])
    run(["k3d", "image", "import", *tags, "--cluster", CLUSTER])


def write_release(sha: str) -> Path:
    """Write the release's kustomizations under `deploy/.release/<sha>/` and return that folder."""
    folder = REPO / "deploy" / ".release" / sha
    for path, text in release_files(sha).items():
        (folder / path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (folder / path).write_text(text)
    return folder


def certificate() -> dict[str, str]:
    """Make a certificate for the cluster's names, signed by mkcert's local authority, and return it as Secret data."""
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
        cert, key = Path(folder) / "tls.crt", Path(folder) / "tls.key"
        run(["mkcert", "-cert-file", str(cert), "-key-file", str(key), *CERT_NAMES])
        return {"tls.crt": cert.read_text(), "tls.key": key.read_text()}


def ensure_secrets() -> None:
    """Create the namespace and each Secret that does not exist yet; existing ones, including your own, are kept."""
    if not succeeds(["kubectl", "get", "namespace", NAMESPACE]):
        run(["kubectl", "create", "namespace", NAMESPACE])
    # Hex keeps the password safe inside DATABASE_URL.
    wanted = {
        "todo-db": lambda: ({"password": secrets.token_hex(24)}, "Opaque"),
        "todo-api": lambda: ({"jwt-secret": secrets.token_hex(32)}, "Opaque"),
        "todo-tls": lambda: (certificate(), "kubernetes.io/tls"),
    }
    for name, make in wanted.items():
        if succeeds(["kubectl", "get", "secret", name, "-n", NAMESPACE]):
            continue
        data, kind = make()
        command, payload = create_secret(name, data, kind)
        run(command, stdin=payload)


def up(sha: str) -> None:
    """Run every step, from the cluster to a rolled-out app."""
    require_tools()
    ensure_cluster()
    build(sha)
    ensure_secrets()
    write_release(sha)
    for step in rollout_steps(sha):
        run(step)
    print(f"\ntodo-app {sha} is running at {URL}", file=sys.stderr)


def main() -> None:
    """Parse the subcommand and run it."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("command", choices=("up", "build", "render", "secrets", "down"))
    parser.add_argument("--sha", help="the commit to deploy (default: the checked-out one)")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    sha = args.sha or current_sha()
    actions = {
        "up": lambda: up(sha),
        "build": lambda: build(sha),
        "render": lambda: print(write_release(sha)),
        "secrets": ensure_secrets,
        "down": lambda: run(["k3d", "cluster", "delete", CLUSTER]),
    }
    try:
        actions[args.command]()
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as error:
        sys.exit(f"stopped: {' '.join(error.cmd)} exited with {error.returncode}")


if __name__ == "__main__":

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Deploy the app to a local k3d cluster: `python3 deploy/k3d/deploy.py up`, then open https://localhost:8443.

`up` creates the cluster if it is missing, builds and imports the images for the current commit, creates the
secrets if they are missing, then applies Postgres, the migration Job and the app, each after the one before is
ready. `build`, `render` and `secrets` run one of those steps alone; `down` deletes the cluster and its data.
Every command is printed before it runs. Secret values reach kubectl on stdin and are never printed or kept.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
import secrets
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
CLUSTER = "todo"
NAMESPACE = "todo"
CLUSTER_CONFIG = "deploy/k3d/cluster.yaml"
PARTS = ("platform", "migrate", "app")
# Each image and the folder it is built from, the same build compose runs.
IMAGES = {"todo-api": "backend", "todo-web": "frontend"}
SHORT_SHA = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{7,40}")
# The browser's address, and the name k6 uses to reach the cluster from inside Docker.
CERT_NAMES = ("localhost", "127.0.0.1", "::1", "host.docker.internal")
TOOLS = ("docker", "k3d", "kubectl", "mkcert")
URL = "https://localhost:8443"


def release_files(sha: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Return the kustomization for each part of a release, keyed by its path under `deploy/.release/<sha>/`.

    Each part builds on its k3d overlay and pins both images to the commit. The migration Job's name also
    carries the commit, so each release runs it once and a repeat deploy of the same commit changes nothing.
    """
    if not SHORT_SHA.fullmatch(sha):
        raise ValueError(f"not a short lowercase git sha: {sha!r}")
    images = "".join(f"  - name: {name}\n    newTag: {sha}\n" for name in IMAGES)

    def kustomization(part: str) -> str:
        suffix = f"nameSuffix: -{sha}\n" if part == "migrate" else ""
        return (
            "apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1\nkind: Kustomization\n"
            f"resources:\n  - ../../../overlays/k3d/{part}\n{suffix}images:\n{images}"
        )

    return {f"{part}/kustomization.yaml": kustomization(part) for part in PARTS}


def rollout_steps(sha: str) -> list[list[str]]:
    """Return the kubectl commands that roll out a written release, each waiting for the one before."""
    release = f"deploy/.release/{sha}"
    namespace = ["-n", NAMESPACE]
    return [
        ["kubectl", "apply", "-k", f"{release}/platform"],
        ["kubectl", "rollout", "status", "statefulset/db", *namespace, "--timeout=180s"],
        ["kubectl", "apply", "-k", f"{release}/migrate"],
        ["kubectl", "wait", "--for=condition=complete", f"job/migrate-{sha}", *namespace, "--timeout=180s"],
        ["kubectl", "apply", "-k", f"{release}/app"],
        ["kubectl", "rollout", "status", "deployment/api", *namespace, "--timeout=300s"],
        ["kubectl", "rollout", "status", "deployment/web", *namespace, "--timeout=180s"],
    ]


def create_secret(name: str, data: dict[str, str], kind: str = "Opaque") -> tuple[list[str], str]:
    """Return the command that creates a Secret and the manifest to send on its stdin, so no value is an argument."""
    manifest = {
        "apiVersion": "v1",
        "kind": "Secret",
        "metadata": {"name": name, "namespace": NAMESPACE},
        "type": kind,
        "stringData": data,
    }
    return ["kubectl", "create", "-f", "-"], json.dumps(manifest)


def run(command: list[str], stdin: str | None = None) -> None:
    """Print the command, run it from the repo root, and stop the deploy if it fails."""
    print("+ " + " ".join(command), file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
    subprocess.run(command, cwd=REPO, input=stdin, text=True, check=True)


def succeeds(command: list[str]) -> bool:
    """Run a read-only check quietly and say whether it succeeded."""
    return subprocess.run(command, cwd=REPO, capture_output=True).returncode == 0


def current_sha() -> str:
    """Return the short sha of the checked-out commit, the tag compose gives its images too."""
    return subprocess.run(
        ["git", "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"], cwd=REPO, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True
    ).stdout.strip()


def require_tools() -> None:
    """Stop with the install command when a tool the deploy needs is missing."""
    missing = [tool for tool in TOOLS if shutil.which(tool) is None]
    if missing:
        sys.exit(f"missing {', '.join(missing)}: brew install {' '.join(missing)} (see the README)")


def ensure_cluster() -> None:
    """Create the three-node cluster unless it already exists."""
    if not succeeds(["k3d", "cluster", "get", CLUSTER]):
        run(["k3d", "cluster", "create", "--config", CLUSTER_CONFIG])


def build(sha: str) -> None:
    """Build both images for the commit and copy them onto every node, so no pod pulls from a registry."""
    tags = [f"{name}:{sha}" for name in IMAGES]
    for tag, folder in zip(tags, IMAGES.values()):
        run(["docker", "build", "-t", tag, folder])
    run(["k3d", "image", "import", *tags, "--cluster", CLUSTER])


def write_release(sha: str) -> Path:
    """Write the release's kustomizations under `deploy/.release/<sha>/` and return that folder."""
    folder = REPO / "deploy" / ".release" / sha
    for path, text in release_files(sha).items():
        (folder / path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (folder / path).write_text(text)
    return folder


def certificate() -> dict[str, str]:
    """Make a certificate for the cluster's names, signed by mkcert's local authority, and return it as Secret data."""
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
        cert, key = Path(folder) / "tls.crt", Path(folder) / "tls.key"
        run(["mkcert", "-cert-file", str(cert), "-key-file", str(key), *CERT_NAMES])
        return {"tls.crt": cert.read_text(), "tls.key": key.read_text()}


def ensure_secrets() -> None:
    """Create the namespace and each Secret that does not exist yet; existing ones, including your own, are kept."""
    if not succeeds(["kubectl", "get", "namespace", NAMESPACE]):
        run(["kubectl", "create", "namespace", NAMESPACE])
    # Hex keeps the password safe inside DATABASE_URL.
    wanted = {
        "todo-db": lambda: ({"password": secrets.token_hex(24)}, "Opaque"),
        "todo-api": lambda: ({"jwt-secret": secrets.token_hex(32)}, "Opaque"),
        "todo-tls": lambda: (certificate(), "kubernetes.io/tls"),
    }
    for name, make in wanted.items():
        if succeeds(["kubectl", "get", "secret", name, "-n", NAMESPACE]):
            continue
        data, kind = make()
        command, payload = create_secret(name, data, kind)
        run(command, stdin=payload)


def up(sha: str) -> None:
    """Run every step, from the cluster to a rolled-out app."""
    require_tools()
    ensure_cluster()
    build(sha)
    ensure_secrets()
    write_release(sha)
    for step in rollout_steps(sha):
        run(step)
    print(f"\ntodo-app {sha} is running at {URL}", file=sys.stderr)


def main() -> None:
    """Parse the subcommand and run it."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("command", choices=("up", "build", "render", "secrets", "down"))
    parser.add_argument("--sha", help="the commit to deploy (default: the checked-out one)")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    sha = args.sha or current_sha()
    actions = {
        "up": lambda: up(sha),
        "build": lambda: build(sha),
        "render": lambda: print(write_release(sha)),
        "secrets": ensure_secrets,
        "down": lambda: run(["k3d", "cluster", "delete", CLUSTER]),
    }
    try:
        actions[args.command]()
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as error:
        sys.exit(f"stopped: {' '.join(error.cmd)} exited with {error.returncode}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

  name: db

metadata:
  name: db
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: db
spec:
  serviceName: db
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: db
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: db
    spec:
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      securityContext:
        # 70 is the postgres user in the Alpine image.
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 70
        runAsGroup: 70
        fsGroup: 70
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault
      containers:
        - name: postgres
          image: postgres:18.6-alpine3.24
          env:
            - name: POSTGRES_USER
              value: todo
            - name: POSTGRES_DB
              value: todo
            - name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD

                  key: password

              containerPort: 5432
          readinessProbe:
            exec:
              command: ["pg_isready", "-U", "todo", "-d", "todo"]

          livenessProbe:
            tcpSocket:
              port: postgres
            periodSeconds: 10
            failureThreshold: 6
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 250m
              memory: 256Mi
            limits:
              cpu: "2"

          emptyDir: {}

    - metadata:

        accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]

# Runs the migrations once per release, with the API image; the deploy waits for it before rolling out the API.
# It gets the database address alone, never the JWT secret.
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: migrate
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: migrate
spec:
  backoffLimit: 2
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 300
  # Kept a week for its logs. Running the same release again after that finds nothing left to migrate.
  ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 604800
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: migrate
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 10001
        runAsGroup: 10001
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault
      containers:
        - name: migrate
          image: todo-api
          command: ["alembic", "upgrade", "head"]
          env:
            - name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: todo-db
                  key: password
            # Kubernetes fills in $(POSTGRES_PASSWORD) from the variable above.
            - name: DATABASE_URL
              value: postgresql+asyncpg://todo:$(POSTGRES_PASSWORD)@db:5432/todo
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 128Mi
            limits:
              cpu: "1"
              memory: 256Mi
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            capabilities:
              drop: [ALL]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: tmp
              mountPath: /tmp
      volumes:
        - name: tmp
          emptyDir: {}

# The API: three pods, one uvicorn process each, one per node. Any pod serves any request.
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: api
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: api
  strategy:
    # A new pod is ready before an old one leaves, so three keep serving through a release.
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 1
      maxUnavailable: 0
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: api
    spec:
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      # Covers the 20 s preStop sleep, uvicorn's 20 s drain and a margin.
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 45
      topologySpreadConstraints:
        - maxSkew: 1
          topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
          whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
          labelSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app.kubernetes.io/name: api
          # Counts only pods of the same release, so a rolling update can always place its new pod.
          matchLabelKeys: [pod-template-hash]
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 10001
        runAsGroup: 10001
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault
      containers:
        - name: api
          image: todo-api
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 8000
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: todo-config
          env:
            - name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: todo-db
                  key: password
            # Kubernetes fills in $(POSTGRES_PASSWORD) from the variable above.
            - name: DATABASE_URL
              value: postgresql+asyncpg://todo:$(POSTGRES_PASSWORD)@db:5432/todo
            - name: JWT_SECRET
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: todo-api
                  key: jwt-secret
          startupProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /livez
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 2
            failureThreshold: 30
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /livez
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 10
            failureThreshold: 3
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /readyz
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 5
            failureThreshold: 2
          lifecycle:
            # Kubernetes takes the pod out of the Service at once, but nginx re-reads DNS only every 10 s and
            # the cluster DNS caches for 5 s. Serving 20 s more covers that, then SIGTERM starts uvicorn's drain.
            # https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/container-lifecycle-hooks/#hook-handler-implementations
            preStop:
              sleep:
                seconds: 20
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 500m
              memory: 256Mi
            # One core is the most a single uvicorn process can use.
            limits:
              cpu: "1"
              memory: 512Mi
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            capabilities:
              drop: [ALL]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: tmp
              mountPath: /tmp
      volumes:
        - name: tmp
          emptyDir: {}
---
# Headless: DNS answers with every ready pod, so nginx balances each request across them itself
# instead of holding kept-alive connections to whichever pod one virtual IP picked.
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: api
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: api
spec:
  clusterIP: None
  selector:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: api
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 8000
      targetPort: http
---
# A drained node or a voluntary eviction never leaves fewer than two pods serving.
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: api
spec:
  minAvailable: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: api

# nginx: serves the SPA, sets the security headers and forwards /api/ to the API pods, as in compose.
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: web
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: web
  strategy:
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 1
      maxUnavailable: 0
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: web
    spec:
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      topologySpreadConstraints:
        - maxSkew: 1
          topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
          whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
          labelSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app.kubernetes.io/name: web
      securityContext:
        # 101 is the nginx user in the unprivileged image.
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 101
        runAsGroup: 101
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: todo-web
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 8080
          env:
            # The full name, because nginx's resolver does not use the pod's DNS search list.
            - name: API_HOST
              value: api.todo.svc.cluster.local
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 5
          livenessProbe:
            tcpSocket:
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 10
          lifecycle:
            # Traefik follows the Service's endpoints directly, so a short pause covers it.
            preStop:
              sleep:
                seconds: 5
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 32Mi
            limits:
              cpu: "1"
              memory: 128Mi
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            capabilities:
              drop: [ALL]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: tmp
              mountPath: /tmp
            # The image's entrypoint writes the filled-in upstream config here at start.
            - name: conf
              mountPath: /etc/nginx/conf.d
      volumes:
        - name: tmp
          emptyDir: {}
        - name: conf
          emptyDir: {}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: web
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: web
spec:
  selector:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: web
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 8080
      targetPort: http
---
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  minAvailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:

# The API: three pods, one uvicorn process each, one per node. Any pod serves any request.
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: api
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: api
  strategy:
    # A new pod is ready before an old one leaves, so three keep serving through a release.
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 1
      maxUnavailable: 0
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: api
    spec:
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      # Covers the 20 s preStop sleep, uvicorn's 20 s drain and a margin.
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 45
      topologySpreadConstraints:
        - maxSkew: 1
          topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
          whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
          labelSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app.kubernetes.io/name: api
          # Counts only pods of the same release, so a rolling update can always place its new pod.
          matchLabelKeys: [pod-template-hash]
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 10001
        runAsGroup: 10001
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault
      containers:
        - name: api
          image: todo-api
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 8000
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: todo-config
          env:
            - name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: todo-db
                  key: password
            # Kubernetes fills in $(POSTGRES_PASSWORD) from the variable above.
            - name: DATABASE_URL
              value: postgresql+asyncpg://todo:$(POSTGRES_PASSWORD)@db:5432/todo
            - name: JWT_SECRET
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: todo-api
                  key: jwt-secret
          startupProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /livez
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 2
            failureThreshold: 30
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /livez
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 10
            failureThreshold: 3
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /readyz
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 5
            failureThreshold: 2
          lifecycle:
            # Kubernetes takes the pod out of the Service at once, but nginx re-reads DNS only every 10 s and
            # the cluster DNS caches for 5 s. Serving 20 s more covers that, then SIGTERM starts uvicorn's drain.
            # https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/container-lifecycle-hooks/#hook-handler-implementations
            preStop:
              sleep:
                seconds: 20
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 500m
              memory: 256Mi
            # One core is the most a single uvicorn process can use.
            limits:
              cpu: "1"
              memory: 512Mi
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            capabilities:
              drop: [ALL]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: tmp
              mountPath: /tmp
      volumes:
        - name: tmp
          emptyDir: {}
---
# Headless: DNS answers with every ready pod, so nginx balances each request across them itself
# instead of holding kept-alive connections to whichever pod one virtual IP picked.
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: api
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: api
spec:
  clusterIP: None
  selector:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: api
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 8000
      targetPort: http
---
# A drained node or a voluntary eviction never leaves fewer than two pods serving.
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: api
spec:
  minAvailable: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: api

          topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
