## Given more time

In priority order. [`FUTURE.md`](FUTURE.md) has the detail.

**How long.** These estimates are for the way this app was built: an AI agent writes the code and the tests, and the lead plans, decides and reviews. A *session* is one or two hours of that pair working together. On top of each estimate, every pull request needs about 30 minutes of the lead's review, the figure from this build. Waits we don't control, such as cloud setup or user testing, are named separately.

| # | What | Why | How long |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Create tasks by describing them**, in text or by voice | The user says what they need, and the app writes the task; one simple way in | About 2 sessions: an AI layer over the existing task service, one endpoint, a voice and text box on the list; 2 to 3 PRs |
| 2 | **Update tasks by voice**: a button, then "mark the report done and move the dentist to Monday" | The same agent, with tools to edit, complete and move tasks | 1 to 2 sessions on top of #1; 1 to 2 PRs |
| 3 | **Ask about your work, with memory**: "summarise my backlog", "what does my week look like?"; the AI remembers what you tell it about yourself | A to-do manager that knows its user | About 2 sessions: a memory table and migration, 1 to 2 endpoints, a summary screen; 2 to 3 PRs |
| 4 | **Tools behind an MCP server**, if the app becomes part of a bigger product | The tools then scale and change apart from the model | About 1 session when it is needed; 1 PR |
| 5 | **API management in front of the models** (Azure API Management or the same on another cloud) | It picks a working model, retries and rate-limits, so the backend doesn't | About 1 session to wire up, plus the cloud setup |
| 6 | **CI/CD with dev, UAT and prod environments**, and the app on a cloud cluster with **Terraform** and the existing Kubernetes manifests (AKS, EKS or GKE) | Versioned releases that move from dev to UAT to prod; start with dev, add UAT when there are users to test with | 2 to 3 sessions: Terraform modules, a cloud overlay, a deploy workflow; 3 to 4 PRs. Waits: cloud setup and approvals |
| 7 | **Decide where the database lives**: in the cluster or managed (Azure Database for PostgreSQL, Cosmos DB, or the same elsewhere) | Managed brings replicas, backups and a connection pooler; in the cluster is portable and cheap | A team discussion first; then about 1 session |

# AI transcripts for todo-app

This branch holds the full record of how the app was built with AI. The code is on [`main`](https://github.com/oneconsciousness/todo-app). This branch has only the transcripts and this guide.

The app was built by an AI agent (Claude Code, with Claude Opus) working with the lead, who set the direction, made the decisions and reviewed every pull request. The lead's words and decisions are also collected in [`docs/kickoff.md`](https://github.com/oneconsciousness/todo-app/blob/main/docs/kickoff.md) on `main`, and the time taken is in the README's "How it was made" section.

## What is here

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `session/fa9c58ff-72fc-4042-9fe7-6e07e6e2c359.jsonl` | The main session, from the first message on Sunday 18 October 2026 to the submission: every message from the lead, every reply and every tool call by the agent, and every result |
| `session/fa9c58ff-72fc-4042-9fe7-6e07e6e2c359/subagents/` | The helper agents the main agent started: reviewers, a docs keeper, and builders for parts of the work |
| `session/fa9c58ff-72fc-4042-9fe7-6e07e6e2c359/tool-results/` | Tool outputs too long to keep inline in the main file |

It is one session. When the conversation grew long, Claude Code summarised the earlier part and carried on in the same file, so nothing was lost; a hook also saved a copy before every summary.

## How to read it

Each file is JSON Lines: one event per line, each with a `timestamp`.

- `"type": "user"` with plain text is the lead typing. `"type": "user"` holding a `tool_result` is the output of a tool the agent ran.
- `"type": "assistant"` is the agent: its replies, and its tool calls (`tool_use`) such as running tests, editing files or opening PRs.

To list the lead's messages with their times:

```bash
python3 -c '
import json, sys
for line in open(sys.argv[1]):
    e = json.loads(line)
    c = e.get("message", {}).get("content")
    if e.get("type") == "user" and isinstance(c, str):
        print(e["timestamp"], c[:120].replace("\n", " "))
' session/fa9c58ff-72fc-4042-9fe7-6e07e6e2c359.jsonl
```

## Before it was published

The files were scanned for secrets: private keys, cloud and GitHub tokens, API keys, JWTs, session cookies and passwords. Nothing real was found: the hits were test strings, the public example values from `.env.example`, and image digests. The secrets used by the app were never read or printed by the agent. The lead chose to publish the transcripts as they are.
